reason: Clear broken cell fragments from the cut to prepare the wound for repair.

effect: The debris is cleared, and the wound now has slots for supply, surface and support.
reaction: It makes sense that the white cells engulfed the fragments; I'm curious how the three repairs fit together.

reason: Add the new cells to the cleared wound to work toward closing its surface.

reason: Use the clot-clearing enzymes on the wound; it is the only offered combination and matches the new goal.
expectation: I expect the enzymes to break down the temporary clot while the repaired tissue remains.

effect: The clot was mostly cleared, leaving closed skin, supporting fibres and a small scar; all goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast between temporary clot threads and lasting support made the ending clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Closing the surface while seeing the deeper tissue still needed repair made healing feel like more than just sealing a cut.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making and then placing each repair component became a little repetitive, even though the sequence was understandable.

surprise.text: The new capillary branch joined another vessel so blood could flow through it; I had not pictured how the new supply would connect.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The make-then-place steps had a clear purpose, although they repeated the same pattern.

continue.text: I would continue into another chapter: seeing the separate repairs come together and the temporary clot cleared was satisfying.
